one_line: 12th‑century vachana saints of Karnataka, anchoring the Anubhava Mantapa and the kayaka–ishtalinga movement under the Kalachuris of Kalyana.

appearance.age_look: Basavanna appears in his mid-30s, lean but sturdy; Akka Mahadevi in her early 20s, slight and poised; Allama Prabhu in his late 40s, slim, ascetic and wiry.
appearance.face: Basavanna has an oval face, wheatish complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed short beard and mustache, big earnest anime eyes with a steady, compassionate gaze and a calm half-smile; Akka Mahadevi has a soft heart-shaped face, light-brown complexion, large expressive eyes, straight refined nose, delicate brows and a serene, inward-looking smile; Allama Prabhu has a long face, medium-brown complexion, high cheekbones, thin lips, slightly hollow cheeks, a fine mustache and short goatee, with thoughtful, almost piercing eyes and a meditative, serious expression.
appearance.hair: Basavanna’s hair is black, tied back into a low knot at the nape, with a few loose strands at the temples, and his forehead bears a small, dark ishtalinga mark; Akka Mahadevi’s long black hair is braided into a single thick plait down her back, wrapped with a thin white cotton strip near the end, with a few strands framing her face, and she wears a simple narrow white headband; Allama Prabhu’s black hair is medium-length and wavy, brushed back and tied into a short low bun, with a thin white tilak line on his forehead.
appearance.costume: Basavanna wears a knee-length white cotton angavastra-style upper cloth draped over both shoulders and chest, paired with a saffron-tinted dhoti wrapped to the ankles with a neat front pleat, the cloth plain but with a thin maroon border, and he wears a simple waist-belt cord, a single rudraksha mala around his neck, a small cylindrical leather ishtalinga-holder strapped on a black cord against his chest, and plain leather sandals; Akka Mahadevi is modestly clothed in a full, ankle-length off-white cotton sari with a simple narrow brown border, wrapped in an old Karnataka village style with the pleats in front and the pallu brought over her left shoulder and around her torso for full coverage, and beneath it a short-sleeved plain white blouse, with multiple rudraksha malas around her neck, a small ishtalinga on a black cord at her chest, thin copper bangles on both wrists and small round silver earrings; Allama Prabhu wears a simple dull-ochre knee-length cotton tunic with three-quarter sleeves and a side-tie at the chest, over a plain brown cotton lower cloth (similar to a dhoti) tied to mid-calf, and a darker brown cloth belt, with a single rudraksha mala, an ishtalinga pendant on a black cord, and bare feet with anklet cords but no metal ornament.
appearance.signature: Basavanna carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord in one hand and a small cloth bag at his waist, symbolising his administrative work and vachana-writing; Akka Mahadevi holds a small, simple single-stringed tanpura-like lute (ekatari) made of a brown gourd and pale wood, slung over her shoulder; Allama Prabhu carries a small hand-damru (hourglass drum) with a plain wooden body and simple cloth cords, held lightly in his right hand.

ref_desc: Basavanna is a lean, mid-30s man with tied-back black hair, white upper cloth and saffron dhoti, rudraksha mala and ishtalinga, holding a palm-leaf roll; Akka Mahadevi is a slight young woman in an off-white sari and braid with ekatari; Allama Prabhu is a wiry older man in ochre tunic and brown lower cloth with damru, all in white, saffron and earthy browns.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet featuring three fixed characters from 12th-century Karnataka, each clearly separated but shown head-to-toe: Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi and Allama Prabhu. Basavanna is a lean man in his mid-30s with an oval face, wheatish skin, short beard and mustache, and large earnest eyes; his black hair is tied in a low knot with a small dark ishtalinga mark on his forehead. He wears a plain white cotton upper cloth draped over both shoulders and chest, and a saffron-tinted dhoti wrapped to his ankles with a thin maroon border, a simple waist-cord, a single rudraksha mala and a small cylindrical leather ishtalinga-holder on a black cord at his chest, plus plain leather sandals; in his hand he holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript and a small cloth bag hangs at his waist. Akka Mahadevi is a slight young woman with a heart-shaped face, light-brown complexion and large expressive eyes, her long black hair braided into a single thick plait wrapped near the end with a narrow white strip and a simple narrow white headband; she wears a modest, ankle-length off-white cotton sari with a narrow brown border, wrapped to cover her fully with the pallu brought around her torso, over a plain short-sleeved white blouse, several rudraksha malas and an ishtalinga on a black cord at her chest, thin copper bangles and small round silver earrings, bare-footed, holding a simple brown-and-pale-wood ekatari (single-stringed lute) slung over her shoulder. Allama Prabhu is a wiry man in his late 40s with a long face, medium-brown skin, high cheekbones, thin mustache and small goatee, wavy black hair tied into a short low bun and a thin white tilak on his forehead; he wears a dull-ochre knee-length cotton tunic with three-quarter sleeves and a side-tie, a plain brown cotton lower cloth tied to mid-calf with a darker brown cloth belt, a single rudraksha mala and an ishtalinga pendant on a black cord, bare feet with simple anklet cords, and he holds a small wooden hand-damru with cloth cords. Use a restrained palette of white, saffron, brown, maroon and warm earthy tones, and show the characters front-facing with clear views of face, hairstyle, full garments, jewellery and their respective palm-leaf roll, ekatari and damru props.
